title: BIO 201 ( UNIZIK ) : MENDELIAN GENETICS AND TERMINOLOGIES
subject: BIO 201

questions.question: Genes are best described as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Genes are the basic units of inheritance located on chromosomes.

questions.question: Chromosomes are which of the following?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are thread-like structures that carry genes.

questions.question: An allele is best defined as which of the following?
questions.explanation: An allele is one of the alternative forms of a gene.

questions.question: The locus of a gene refers to which of the following?
questions.explanation: A locus is the position of a gene along a chromosome.

questions.question: Homozygous condition involves which of the following?
questions.explanation: Homozygous means two copies of the same allele at a locus.

questions.question: Heterozygous condition involves which of the following?
questions.explanation: Heterozygous means two different alleles at a given locus.

questions.question: Phenotype refers to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Phenotype refers to the observable characteristics of an organism.

questions.question: Genotype refers to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Genotype is the genetic constitution of an organism.

questions.question: ABO blood group system is controlled by how many alleles?
questions.explanation: The ABO system is controlled by three alleles represented as A B and O.

questions.question: A mating of AO and BO can produce which blood groups?
questions.explanation: AO and BO parents can produce offspring of groups A B AB and O.

questions.question: Joseph Kolreuter carried out artificial hybridization in which year?
questions.explanation: Kolreuter performed early artificial hybridization work in 1760.

questions.question: Gregor Mendel is known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mendel is regarded as the father of modern genetics.

questions.question: Population genetics studies the frequency and interaction of alleles and genes in which group?
questions.explanation: Population genetics studies allele and gene frequencies in populations.

questions.question: Molecular genetics studies genes at which level?
questions.explanation: Molecular genetics studies gene structure and function at the molecular level.

questions.question: Genetic engineering is also known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering is also called recombinant DNA technology.

questions.question: The Human Genome Project mapped all human genes in which year?
questions.explanation: The Human Genome Project mapped human genes successfully in 2003.

questions.question: BRCA gene abnormalities increase the risk of which cancer?
questions.explanation: BRCA gene abnormalities are linked to breast and ovarian cancers.

questions.question: Genetic fingerprinting is most useful for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Genetic fingerprinting can be used to determine paternity in disputed cases.

questions.question: Monohybrid inheritance studies how many pairs of contrasting characteristics?
questions.explanation: Monohybrid inheritance involves one pair of contrasting characteristics.

questions.question: The F2 monohybrid ratio for tall to dwarf is which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mendel observed an approximate three to one ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.question: Dihybrid inheritance involves how many pairs of contrasting characteristics?
questions.explanation: Dihybrid inheritance involves two pairs of contrasting characteristics.

questions.question: Mendel's principle of independent assortment states that one pair of characteristics may combine with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Independent assortment allows one pair of characteristics to combine with another pair.

questions.question: Chromosomes are composed primarily of DNA and which other substance?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made up of DNA and proteins.

questions.question: Histones are rich in which amino acids?
questions.explanation: Histones are basic proteins rich in lysine and arginine.

questions.question: The nucleolus is the site of synthesis of which molecule?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of ribonucleic acid synthesis.

questions.question: Human somatic cells contain how many chromosomes?
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells contain 46 chromosomes.

questions.question: Nondisjunction can produce an organism with which condition?
questions.explanation: Nondisjunction can produce an organism with an extra chromosome.

questions.question: A translocation occurs when a chromosome part attaches to which type of chromosome?
questions.explanation: A translocation involves attachment of a chromosome part to a nonhomologous chromosome.

questions.question: An inversion involves a chromosome segment being cut out and which action?
questions.explanation: In an inversion a chromosome segment is cut out and reversed.

questions.question: The XX-XY sex determining system is found in which group?
questions.explanation: The XX-XY system occurs in mammals and some plants.

questions.question: The ZZ-ZW sex determining system is found in which group?
questions.explanation: The ZZ-ZW system occurs in birds fish snakes and butterflies.

questions.question: Bridges proposed that the ratio of X chromosomes to autosome sets determines which feature?
questions.explanation: Bridges 1925 proposed the genic balance theory in which the sex index determines sex.

questions.question: Males are hemizygous for X-linked genes because they are which sex?
questions.explanation: Males have a single copy of X-linked genes and are called hemizygous.

questions.question: A male with an X-linked disorder transmits the gene to which offspring?
questions.explanation: A father transmits his X chromosome to all daughters but not to sons.

questions.question: A Y-linked disorder is transmitted from father to which offspring?
questions.explanation: Y-linked genes are passed from father to sons.

questions.question: Albinism is associated with absence or defect of which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Albinism results from absence or defect of tyrosinase.

questions.question: Phenylketonuria involves a mutation in the gene for which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Phenylketonuria is caused by mutation in the gene for phenylalanine hydroxylase.

questions.question: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a mutation in the gene for which protein?
questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis results from mutation in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator gene.

questions.question: Sickle cell trait provides resistance against which disease?
questions.explanation: Sickle cell trait gives partial protection against malaria.

questions.question: The double helix structure of DNA was described by which scientists?
questions.explanation: Watson and Crick described the DNA double helix in 1953.

questions.question: RNA contains which nitrogenous base instead of thymine?
questions.explanation: RNA contains uracil in place of the thymine found in DNA.

questions.question: The central dogma of molecular biology describes information flow from which molecule?
questions.explanation: The central dogma states that genetic information flows from DNA to RNA to protein.

questions.question: Which codons act as termination signals during translation?
questions.explanation: UAA UAG and UGA are nonsense codons that stop translation.

questions.question: Somatic mutations are generally which of the following?
questions.explanation: Somatic mutations occur in nonreproductive cells and are not passed to offspring.

questions.question: Point mutation involves a change in which unit?
questions.explanation: A point mutation involves a change in a single nucleotide or base pair.

questions.question: Deletion mutation results in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Deletion mutation involves loss of a portion of a chromosome or gene.

questions.question: Induced mutations are caused by agents known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mutagens are physical or chemical agents that induce mutations.

questions.question: Lamarck proposed that organisms transmit which characteristics to offspring?
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed inheritance of acquired characteristics.

questions.question: Darwin proposed which mechanism for organic evolution?
questions.explanation: Darwin proposed natural selection as the mechanism of evolution.

questions.question: Darwin's theory states that living organisms produce which of the following?
questions.explanation: Darwin noted that organisms produce more offspring than can survive.
